A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TeamTR and contain the same main sections and Appendices A–H. Their text, equations, figures, and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G report original benchmark evaluations, training diagnostics, ablations, scaling experiments, and agent-replacement results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the original empirical evaluations and analyses, including numerical tables and training curves.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, intermediate-occupancy resampling, per-agent token-KL constraints, group-normalized objectives, and Stage-0 replacement alignment are unchanged, including their appendix formulations.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training data and evaluation coverage: AIME 2024/2025, MATH-500, ZebraLogic, AutoLogi, AR-Bench, PlanBench, and the tool-mediated τ-bench scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout the tables and figures, including GRPO/DAPO single-agent baselines, PPO/GRPO/DAPO sequential baselines, debate and role-play methods, strong models, and replacement controls. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices G–H retain identical model configurations, sampling budgets, evaluation metrics, benchmark subsets, and testing procedures. Training settings and the 500-context replacement-alignment protocol are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The resampling, trust-region, update-order, advantage-estimation, and protocol-unification ablations are retained unchanged. Scaling, certificate calibration, token-level shifts, KL-monitor reliability, and importance-weight degeneracy analyses also match.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same three-seed mean and standard deviation practice in Appendix G, seed-variation shading in Figure 3, correlation interval in Figure 4, and token-KL subsampling statistics.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted curves, rankings, and reported findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains homogeneous TeamTR's 88.1% AIME24 and 99.3% MATH-500 scores, and Table 9 retains all ablation results.

T1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices B–F preserve the same definitions, assumptions, bounds, propositions, and proofs, including quadratic-versus-linear occupancy penalties, improvement certificates, replacement guarantees, and finite-sample analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about compounding occupancy shift, quadratic-to-linear penalty reduction, improvement lower bounds, empirical gains, and plug-and-play replacement. The abstract's 7.1% average improvement claim is unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are unchanged, including the single-active-agent restriction, the diagnostic status of empirical certificates, dependence on estimation-error proxies, and the absence of a guarantee for the replacement step itself.

D1.justification: Implementation notes, hyperparameters, token-KL monitoring, alignment instructions, tokenizer checks, and the code-access destination are unchanged. Bibliographic URL rewrapping changes presentation without introducing a new resource or access procedure.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A revise citations: v2 adds SAT and DICE by Xie et al. (2026a,b) and Beyond Compilation by Zhang et al. (2026), while removing Chen et al.'s FireAct, Lowe et al. (2017), and Singhal et al. (2023). These substitutions leave the surrounding positioning arguments largely unchanged and add no substantive comparative discussion.

P1.justification: V2 adds Siyang Cao to the author list and introduces running-title text. Citation-related text edits are localized; the section order, narrative structure, and scientific prose remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: V2 adds running headers and reflows bibliography entries and URLs. On page 11, the DeepScaleR URL now wraps within its column instead of overlapping adjacent references and extending beyond the page. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 makes a limited, visible readability improvement by fixing the overflowing DeepScaleR bibliography URL on page 11, restoring unobscured reference text. The scientific evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged. Citation substitutions add no substantive analysis, so the demonstrated quality gain is confined to presentation.
